questions.question: A ball starts from rest and slides down a \(30^\circ\) incline. After \(4\ \text{s}\) its speed reaches \(6\ \text{m/s}\). Assuming constant acceleration along the plane, how far will the block travel in the next  \(6\ \text{s}\)?

A test vehicle moves along a circular ramp of radius \(r=40\ \text{m}\). At the instant of interest its speed is \(v=18\ \text{m/s}\), and it is still accelerating tangentially with angular acceleration  \(\alpha=0.5\ \text{rad/s}^2\). Determine the magnitude of the acceleration (in \(\text{m/s}^2\)).

A block initially at rest is acted upon by a constant horizontal force of \(18\ \text{N}\) for \(3\ \text{s}\). After the force is removed, the block continues to move at a constant velocity and covers a distance of \(80\ \text{m}\) during the following \(10\ \text{s}\). Determine the mass of the block in kilograms.

A soccer ball is kicked from level ground with initial speed \(v_0 = 40\ \text{m/s}\) at an angle \(\theta = 45^\circ\) above the horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\). Find the horizontal range \(R\).

Two particles start from the same location at the same instant and move in a straight line. Particle A has initial speed \(u_A = 6\ \text{m/s}\) and constant acceleration \(a_A = 1.5\ \text{m/s}^2\). Particle B has initial speed \(u_B = 2\ \text{m/s}\) and constant acceleration \(a_B = 2.5\ \text{m/s}^2\). They arrive at the same point at the same time. How long (in seconds) do they travel?
A car is traveling along a straight highway at a speed of \(72\ \text{km/h}\). It comes to rest uniformly in a distance of \(200\ \text{m}\). Find the stopping time \(t\) in seconds.

A small drone is flying north with a speed of \(36\ \text{km/h}\). A steady wind suddenly blows toward the east, perpendicular to the drone’s motion. After the wind begins to act, the drone’s resultant ground speed becomes \(45\ \text{km/h}\). What is the magnitude of the wind’s velocity component?

A small remote-controlled boat needs to cross a 120 m wide lake. In still air, the boat can travel straight across in 3 minutes. However, when a steady crosswind begins to blow, the boat must aim slightly into the wind in order to reach a point directly opposite its starting location. Under these conditions, it takes 4 minutes to cross. What is the wind’s velocity in m/min?
A cyclist rides from home to a lakeside trail at \(12\ \text{mph}\) and returns along the same route at \(18\ \text{mph}\). What is the average speed (mph) for the entire round trip?

A small object moves along a straight path with uniform acceleration \(a_0 = 4\ \text{cm/s}^2\). During the 10th second, it travels \(43\ \text{cm}\). Determine the initial velocity \(v_0\) in \(\text{cm/s}\).
A commuter train moves at 54 km/h and comes to rest uniformly in 12 s. Determine how far from the platform the brakes should be applied.

A cargo drone flies horizontally at \(100\ \text{m/s}\) and drops a small package from an altitude of \(300\ \text{m}\). Neglecting air resistance, what will be the package’s speed (m/s) after \(4\ \text{s}\) of free fall? Use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A rescue drone flying horizontally at a constant altitude of \(400\ \text{m}\) releases a supply package with a horizontal speed of \(120\ \text{m/s}\). Neglecting air resistance, how far horizontally (m) will the package travel before it reaches the ground?  Assume \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A drone releases a small package vertically upward from a height with an initial speed of \(10\ \text{m/s}\). After \(4\ \text{s}\), the package reaches the ground. Assuming \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\), find the release height \(h\) (m) of the drone.

A race car moves along a curved test track described by \(y = 0.05\,x^{2}\). At the point where \(x = 200\ \text{m}\), its speed is \(v = 25\ \text{m/s}\) and its tangential acceleration is \(a_t = 3\ \text{m/s}^2\). Determine the magnitude of the acceleration at this instant.
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5 P102, 103:

 Dynamics- Particle Kinematics – Normal and Tangential Components

questions.question:
A delivery drone moves in a horizontal plane with position

\[

(x(t),\,y(t))=\big(0.25\,t^{3},\;0.50\,t^{2}+t\big),

\]

where \(x,y\) are in meters and \(t\) is in seconds. Determine the drone’s

acceleration at \(t=4\ \text{s}\) (give the vector and its magnitude).

A soccer ball is kicked with speed \(v_0 = 35\ \text{m/s}\) at an angle \(\theta = 40^\circ\) above the horizontal.

A stadium wall stands \(x=40\ \text{m}\) away. At what height \(y\) (m) does the ball strike the wall?

Use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A jet cruises horizontally at \(v=200\ \text{m/s}\) at an altitude of \(1200\ \text{m}\).

It releases a sensor package with no initial vertical velocity. Determine how long (s) it takes the package to reach the ground.

Take \(g=9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

Vehicle A starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of \(2\ \text{m/s}^2\).

At the same time, and from the same starting line, vehicle B travels in a parallel lane at a constant speed

of \(30\ \text{m/s}\).

After how many seconds will vehicle A overtake vehicle B?

A train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at a rate of \( 8\,\mathrm{m/s^2} \). At the exact moment the train begins to move, a car traveling on a parallel path at a constant velocity of \( 90\,\mathrm{m/s} \) passes it. The time it takes for the train to catch up to and overtake the car is most nearly:

A vehicle is traveling at an initial velocity of \( 30\,\mathrm{mph} \) along a highway acceleration lane. To safely merge into a specific gap in the adjacent traffic lane, the vehicle must travel a longitudinal distance of exactly \( 200\,\mathrm{ft} \) in precisely \( 3.5\,\mathrm{s} \). The constant acceleration (\( \mathrm{ft/s^2} \)) required for the vehicle to achieve this merge is most nearly:

A particle travels along a straight line such that its velocity is defined by the equation \( v(t) = 20 + 5t \), where \( v \) is in meters per second and \( t \) is the time in seconds. The total distance traveled by the particle during the first \( 10\,\mathrm{s} \) is most nearly:

The rectilinear position of a particle moving along a straight path is defined by the time-dependent equation \( s(t) = 30t + 2t^2 – 7t^3 \), where \( s \) is the displacement in meters and \( t \) is the time in seconds. The acceleration of the particle at \( t = 3\,\mathrm{s} \) is most nearly:

A testing vehicle undergoes plane circular motion with a constant radius of \( 150\,\mathrm{m} \) about the origin. The vehicle starts exactly at the \( x \)-axis (\( \theta = 0 \)) at time \( t = 0\,\mathrm{s} \) and travels with a constant transverse velocity of \( 30\,\mathrm{m/s} \). At time \( t = 10\,\mathrm{s} \), the angle \( \theta \) from the \( x \) axis to the position vector \( \mathbf{r} \) is most nearly:

A ball is projected vertically upward from a height of \( 6 \, \mathrm{ft} \) above the ground with an initial velocity of \( 65 \, \mathrm{ft/sec} \). Neglecting air resistance, the maximum height above the ground that the ball will reach is most nearly:

A car is traveling at \( 48 \, \mathrm{mph} \) when the driver sees the traffic light turn yellow. The yellow phase lasts for \( 4.5 \, \mathrm{s} \), and the intersection ahead is \( 160 \, \mathrm{ft} \) wide. What constant acceleration is required for the car to just clear the intersection at the exact moment the light turns red? The acceleration is most nearly:
A car with a mass of \(1500\ \text{kg}\) is traveling at \(72\ \text{km/h}\). If the car comes to a complete stop in \(20\ \text{m}\), determine the average braking force required (in newtons).

Two forces act on a \(0.25\,\text{kg}\) object:

\(\vec F_{1}=4\mathbf i + 3\mathbf j – 5\mathbf k\ \text{N}\)

and

\(\vec F_{2}=-2\mathbf i + 4\mathbf j – \mathbf k\ \text{N}\).

Determine the magnitude of the acceleration of the object in \(\text{m/s}^2\).

A vehicle with a mass of \( 1000\,\mathrm{kg} \) is being towed across a smooth, level surface where friction is considered negligible. The tow rope being used has a maximum tension capacity (breaking strength) of \( 2500\,\mathrm{N} \). The maximum theoretical acceleration the car can experience without the rope snapping is most nearly:
tags: One Dimensional Motion Of A Particle Constant Mass

questions.question: A ball experiences a constant force \(\vec{F} = 6\mathbf i – 4\mathbf j + 3\mathbf k\) N and moves through a displacement \(\vec{s} = 2\mathbf i + \mathbf j – \mathbf k\) m. Determine the work done by the force (in J).

A winch pulls a boat-and-trailer of total mass \(m=900\ \text{kg}\) up a launch ramp that makes an angle  \(\theta=12^\circ\) with the horizontal. The cable reels in so that the boat moves at a steady \(v=0.60\ \text{m/s}\). Neglect rolling resistance and losses. Determine the mechanical power (W) delivered by the winch.
A \(5\ \text{kg}\) object is released from rest and falls freely under gravity. Determine its kinetic energy (in joules) after \(t = 3\ \text{s}\) of fall, neglecting air resistance.

A hoist lifts a load of \(200\ \text{kg}\) vertically upward at a constant speed of \(0.25\ \text{m/s}\). Determine the power output (in J/s) required by the hoist motor. Neglect energy losses and assume steady motion.

A constant horizontal force of \(F = 30\ \text{N}\) pushes a \(1.5\ \text{kg}\) block up a smooth incline that rises \(25^\circ\) above the horizontal. If the block moves a distance of \(5\ \text{m}\) along the incline, find the work done by the horizontal force. Ignore the effect of gravity and friction.
When a spring is compressed by \(10\ \text{cm}\), its potential energy is \(25\ \text{J}\). Determine the force (in newtons) required to compress the same spring by \(25\ \text{cm}\).
A \(12\ \text{kg}\) object is dropped from a height of \(80\ \text{m}\). Neglecting air resistance, determine its kinetic energy (in joules) when it is \(50\ \text{m}\) above the ground.

A \(5\ \text{kg}\) object is released from rest and falls freely under gravity. Assume the initial height is \(h_0 = 50\ \text{m}\) above the ground. Determine its potential energy (J) after \(t = 3\ \text{s}\) of fall (ignore air resistance).

A motor delivers 3.00 kW of power to a pump that lifts water vertically 5.0 m from a well. The overall efficiency of the motor–pump system is 80%. Neglecting losses in the piping, determine the mass of water (in kg) that can be pumped in 1.0 min.

A well is \(10\ \text{m}\) deep and \(2.0\ \text{m}\) in diameter. Only the bottom \(2.0\ \text{m}\) contains water. A pump at the bottom empties the water in \(20\ \text{min}\). Estimate the required power (hp), neglecting losses.
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5 P107:

Dynamics – Principle of Work and Energy – Power and Efficiency

questions.question: A \(1500\,\text{kg}\) car moves down a \(20^\circ\) incline with initial speed \(v_1=14\,\text{m/s}\).Brakes are applied and the car comes to rest uniformly after traveling \(s=30\,\text{m}\) along the slope.Using the nonconservative work–energy relation, find the average braking force \(F_b\) in kN.
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5, P106：

Dynamics – Principle of Work and Energy

questions.question:
A \(6\ \text{kg}\) ball is dropped from a height of \(4\ \text{m}\) onto a soft surface.

The ball continues to move \(0.15\ \text{m}\) into the surface before stopping.

Assuming the resisting force of the surface is constant, determine the average resisting force (in newtons).
A body is dropped freely from a height of \(H = 40\ \text{m}\). At what height \(y\) above the ground will its kinetic energy be three times its remaining potential energy?

A baseball of mass \(0.145\ \text{kg}\) is pitched horizontally toward a batter with a speed of \(38\ \text{m/s}\). Take the direction from the pitcher to the batter as the positive \(x\)-axis. The batter hits the ball, and it leaves the bat with a speed of \(46\ \text{m/s}\) at \(25^\circ\) above the horizontal, traveling back toward the pitcher. Determine the magnitude of the impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered to the ball by the bat.

A \(0.25\ \text{kg}\) soccer ball is moving horizontally toward the west with a speed of \(18\ \text{m/s}\). A player kicks the ball so that it leaves the foot with a speed of \(24\ \text{m/s}\) at an angle of \(40^\circ\) north of east. Determine the magnitude of the net impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered to the ball by the player’s foot.

A \(0.5\ \text{kg}\) drone is flying horizontally toward the east with a speed of \(12\ \text{m/s}\). A sudden gust of wind acts on the drone and changes its velocity to \(15\ \text{m/s}\) at a direction of \(30^\circ\) north of east. Determine the magnitude of the net impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered by the wind to the drone.

A \(3,000\ \text{kg}\) truck is moving north at \(12\ \text{m/s}\). A \(1,500\ \text{kg}\) van is moving south at \(16\ \text{m/s}\) toward the truck. The collision is perfectly inelastic, and the two vehicles stick together. Find the combined velocity (m/s) of the wreckage and specify its travel direction.
questions.answer: \(2.67\ \text{m/s}\) in the travel direction of the truck (north).

questions.question: A \(900\ \text{kg}\) compact car is traveling east at \(22\ \text{m/s}\). A \(1,400\ \text{kg}\) SUV is traveling west at \(18\ \text{m/s}\) toward the compact car. The two vehicles collide and lock together. Determine the magnitude and direction of the combined velocity immediately after impact.
questions.answer: \(2.35\ \text{m/s}\) in the travel direction of the SUV (west).

questions.question: A \(1.2\ \text{kg}\) ball \(A\) moves to the right at \(4.0\ \text{m/s}\) along a smooth, horizontal surface. At the same time, a \(1.8\ \text{kg}\) ball \(B\) moves toward ball \(A\) along the same line at \(3.0\ \text{m/s}\) to the left. The coefficient of restitution between the two balls is \(e = 0.60\). Determine the final velocity (m/s) of ball \(A\) immediately after the collision. Take the original direction of motion of ball \(A\) as positive.

Two spheres, one with a mass of \( 2.0\,\mathrm{kg} \) and the other with a mass of \( 4.0\,\mathrm{kg} \), are traveling towards each other on a frictionless collinear path. Before the head-on collision, the \( 2.0\,\mathrm{kg} \) sphere has a velocity of \( 5.0\,\mathrm{m/s} \) to the right, and the \( 4.0\,\mathrm{kg} \) sphere has a velocity of \( 3.0\,\mathrm{m/s} \) to the left. If the coefficient of restitution (\( e \)) between the two spheres is \( 0.5 \), the final velocities of the spheres immediately after the collision are most nearly:

A cube-shaped block with dimensions of \( 1\,\mathrm{m} \times 1\,\mathrm{m} \times 1\,\mathrm{m} \) is placed on a flat horizontal surface. The block has a density of \( 2,500\,\mathrm{kg/m^3} \). A horizontal force of \( 10\,\mathrm{kN} \) is applied to the centroid of the block. If the coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is \( \mu_s = 0.25 \), which of the following statements is most nearly correct regarding the block’s impending motion?
W

The coefficient of static friction between the block and the incline is \( \mu_s = 0.3 \). Determine the most nearly correct critical angle (\( \theta \)) at which the block begins to slide.
θ

A \( 10 \, \mathrm{kg} \) block starting from rest slides down a \( 28^\circ \) inclined plane. After \( 12 \, \mathrm{s} \), the block reaches a velocity of \( 18 \, \mathrm{m/s} \). Determine the kinetic coefficient of friction between the block and the inclined surface.
